selectedApi: public static System.Threading.Tasks.Task Run(System.Action action, System.Threading.CancellationToken cancellationToken)

upstreamMapping.assertions: Selected Action live-token body invocation and RanToCompletion; no upstream generic/AttachedToParent execution
Selected precanceled Action suppression and IsCanceled; await replaces unsupported public Wait

semantics: Validate action before Java token null
Always queue including requested tokens; no return-time status contract
Worker checks requested token once before invoking action
Cancellation after entry neither interrupts nor forces cancellation
Only associated requested token equal to thrown OCE token cancels; original OCE retained for repeated awaits
Unrequested/default/foreign/null Java OCE token faults; ordinary failures fault despite requests
No Run registration/CTR/timer ownership; completion dispatch outside action catch

fieldNormalization.repeatIdentity: For synthesized skip TaskCanceledException with no original action exception, this is a vacuous original-identity assertion. No synthesized exception object reuse is claimed. Matching action OCE and fault identities are compared directly.
fieldNormalization.taskIdentity: TaskCanceledException payload identity; other exceptions vacuous
fieldNormalization.heldRunning: Only emitted while an entered action is blocked; never status at Run return

javaAdaptations: Java null token validation and null OCE token faults are separate representation controls
No inheritable JVM state from creator at fresh daemon construction is a correction to the predecessor shared helper; it is source-derived predecessor behavior, not an observed predecessor run
Cached workers are not cleared of arbitrary task-written ThreadLocals; no CLR ExecutionContext capture claim
Foreign Java Throwable wrapped with original cause
Rejected executor reports on new daemon and invokes work in finally; catastrophic thread creation failures remain outside delivery guarantee
Private held executor/after-entry barrier gives source-supported ordering, not a CLR scheduling observation
